content:
If you've been using apps on your Apple Watch beta all summer, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating those apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

These updates will be pushed via the App Store, and the version update notes will read: "This app was updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27. No new features."

Apple notified developers this week that the entire process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27, along with iOS 27 and all other new operating systems, is expected to be released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary updates are rolling out just in time.

Apple says this arrangement is necessary because some watchOS apps are experiencing issues on the arm64 architecture. It's understood they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging affected apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue working normally without any action required from developers.
